title: Economic breakdown compiler for routes, models, and tenants
creator: Aditi Verma
description: Implement a service that compiles per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns for both real-time dashboards and daily rollups. The compiler must combine streaming traces (request start/end, kernel timers, GPU seconds), usage envelopes (token counts, embedding units), and model performance profiles (per-token kernel cost, memory overhead) to produce explainable line-item breakdowns usable by the Console and billing insights. This work covers both a low-latency path for near-real-time UI updates and a fault-tolerant batch path for accurate daily aggregates and reconciliations. Core goals: 1) deterministically attribute cost and latency to route, model variant, tenant, and optional tags (route metadata); 2) correctly handle batching, KV cache hits/misses, prefix amortization, and partial streaming responses; 3) be idempotent in the face of duplicate events and resilient to late-arriving telemetry; 4) expose clear schema and confidence metrics so Console can surface inference economics with drilldowns and variance bands.
design_summary: Two-stage architecture: a streaming composer that ingests request traces + kernel telemetry and emits provisional breakdowns to a materialized view for UI; and a daily compiler that consumes canonical event logs + profiling tables to compute final reconciled line-items and provenance (event ids, reconciliation notes). Attribution rules are rule-based with a pluggable 'splitter' function for new cost types (e.g., tool calls, API proxies). Use RocksDB-backed local state in streaming layer for short-window aggregation and BigQuery/warehouse tables for persistent rollups. Ensure idempotency via request_event_id and sequence numbers. Provide a JSON breakdown schema that lists components (gpu_compute, memory_pinning, kv_cache_hit_credit, io, scheduler_wait, overhead) with numeric amounts, units, and confidence tags.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming path returns provisional breakdowns within 2s of final token for 95% of requests in staging under 99th percentile load
Daily rollup matches streaming provisional totals within 0.5% for synthetic workloads and explains deviations with 'late_event' flags

Breakdown schema includes at least these components: gpu_compute, kernel_overhead, queue_wait, kv_cache_credit, prefix_amortization, tooling_invocation_cost, network_io; all components are populated or explicitly zero
Rollup job is idempotent and re-runnable without inflating totals (use deterministic keys)
Console can query per-route/per-model/per-customer breakdowns and display change history; API contract documented
Automated tests cover batching attribution heuristics, kv-cache amortization, and late-event reconciliation
tasks: Write detailed design doc and example breakdown schema (link in comments)
Implement streaming composer: Kafka consumer -> RocksDB state -> provisional emitter
Implement daily compiler: Spark job / dataflow job that joins event log with model_profile and writes final breakdowns to warehouse
Instrument end-to-end tests and synthetic workload generator to validate attribution
Add API endpoints and Console wiring for provisional + reconciled views
Create alerts and SLOs for streaming lag, reconciliation delta, and schema drift

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: late-arriving kernel telemetry can shift costs. Mitigation: tag provisional rows with 'finalized=false' and include 'late_event' provenance in reconciled rows
Risk: batching makes per-request attribution non-trivial. Mitigation: attribute compute by fractional token share using timeline interpolation and record per-request token ranges

Risk: KV cache amortization could double-count savings across tenants if prefix ownership ambiguous. Mitigation: amortize based on observed prefix reuse by tenant-window and expose amortization_amount and amortized_over_n_requests
